Answer: B
Reason: The chest X-ray labeled Figure 3a demonstrates bilateral, multifocal nodular and patchy opacities (often described as acinar shadows) with increased infiltration, which is the characteristic radiographic presentation of the diffuse form of bronchioloalveolar carcinoma (BAC). This contrasts with the solitary nodule pattern seen in localized disease and aligns with the progressive nature shown in the serial images.
